content.intro: Compression and Data Transformation is part of specialized topics and continued learning. This lesson connects node:zlib, Compression streams, Content encoding to a concrete Node.js example. Focus on the behavior you can observe, the assumptions the API makes, and one failure or boundary case.
content.why_it_matters: Database clients manage queries and connections; transactions and parameterized queries protect data integrity. Test concurrent updates, rollback behavior, connection failures, invalid input, and query plans as appropriate.

content_blocks.title: The core idea

items.title: node:zlib
items.text: For node:zlib, identify the relevant Node.js API or runtime behavior, trace its inputs and observable result, then test one invalid input, failure, lifecycle edge, or version-dependent assumption. Avoid inferring correctness from a happy-path run alone.

items.title: Compression streams
items.text: Streams process data incrementally. Backpressure allows a slow consumer to regulate a faster producer instead of accumulating unbounded memory.

items.title: Content encoding
items.text: Buffers store bytes. Text encodings define how byte sequences map to strings, so test byte lengths and conversions with non-ASCII data.

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety note
content_blocks.text: Teaching baseline: use a supported Node.js LTS release (Node.js 24 LTS as checked on 2026-10-13). The official releases page lists Node.js 26 as Current and Node.js 24/22 as LTS. Some advanced APIs, flags, permission behavior, embedded SQLite capabilities, module-loader hooks, and TypeScript integration are version-sensitive; verify the exact installed runtime. The Node.js 22 runtime available in the build-check environment is used only for syntax checks. This example is for learning and static validation, not for executing untrusted learner code inside CodeLeaf.

common_mistakes.problem: Concatenating user input into SQL or holding transactions open while waiting for unrelated network work.
common_mistakes.why: The code may pass a simple demonstration yet fail with real inputs, resource limits, timing, or runtime differences.
common_mistakes.fix: Bind values through the database driver and keep transaction boundaries short and explicit.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a snippet without checking its runtime, dependencies, input assumptions, or cleanup behavior.
common_mistakes.why: Node.js APIs and surrounding ecosystem tools have explicit version, trust, and resource boundaries.
common_mistakes.fix: State the environment and dependency assumptions, then rerun the example from a clean starting state.
